Systems & tooling

Linux Wireless and Driver Debugging

Planned notes on troubleshooting Wi-Fi stacks across firmware, kernel drivers, and IEEE 802.11 packet captures on Linux.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned series documents practical debugging workflows across the Linux wireless stack, combining IEEE 802.11 packet inspection in Wireshark, hostapd test setups, iwlwifi driver logs, and firmware state-transition analysis.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Testbed

  • Define the access point, client, and capture interfaces.
  • Record driver, firmware, and kernel versions.
  • Document the test topology and RF conditions.

Capture setup

  • Configure monitor mode and channel selection.
  • Capture IEEE 802.11 management and data frames.
  • Record filters and capture duration.

Driver and firmware logs

  • Enable the relevant kernel debug channels.
  • Correlate driver events with firmware state transitions.
  • Capture hostapd and supplicant logs.

Failure reproduction

  • Define a minimal reproduction sequence.
  • Repeat the sequence across boots and configurations.
  • Record which variables change the outcome.

Analysis and references

  • Compare observed frames with the expected state machine.
  • State the supported root-cause conclusion.
  • Link the relevant driver and standards documentation.

Topics to cover

  • IEEE 802.11 capture analysis with Wireshark
  • Linux wireless testbeds with hostapd and iwlwifi
  • Kernel and firmware log correlation
  • Diagnosing wireless state-transition failures
